findings.claim: TRUNK-6701 asked for two things on this hot path, and only one shipped: the per-request `String.valueOf(System.currentTimeMillis())` + request-attribute write on line 64 (the ticket's "unused unique-id attribute") is untouched, and nothing in the PR, the code, or the now-Closed ticket records why it was left. Leaving it is the right call, but the reason lives nowhere.
findings.evidence: Ticket TRUNK-6701 (fetched at https://openmrs.atlassian.net/rest/api/2/issue/TRUNK-6701) says under Requested change: 'Only write session attributes when their values actually change, AND remove (or make lazy) the unused unique-id attribute.' The PR delivers the first half only; `git diff eda229b1..d381957e` leaves web/src/main/java/org/openmrs/web/filter/OpenmrsFilter.java:64 unchanged. In-repo, the ticket's premise checks out: `git grep -n INIT_REQ_UNIQUE_ID` over the whole tree returns exactly 2 hits (WebConstants.java:20 declaration, OpenmrsFilter.java:64 write) and zero readers -- positive control: the same pipeline returns 3 files for OPENMRS_USER_CONTEXT_HTTPSESSION_ATTR. But it is a PUBLISHED cross-module request attribute, and `gh search code INIT_REQ_UNIQUE_ID --owner openmrs` finds six downstream readers: openmrs-module-legacyui HtmlIncludeTag.java and PortletController.java, openmrs-module-reporting ReportingPortletController.java, openmrs-module-htmlwidgets HtmlUtil.java, openmrs-module-htmlformflowsheet HtmlIncludeTag.java, openmrs-module-personalhr PortletController.java (plus a redeclaration in openmrs-module-uiframework WebConstants). So removing it would break portlet/htmlInclude caching downstream, and declining the ticket's second ask was correct. The cost left behind is one long->String allocation plus one ServletRequest.setAttribute per top-level HTTP request -- and only per top-level request: I disassembled the resolved spring-web 7.0.9 OncePerRequestFilter.doFilter (javap -c) and confirmed it sets the alreadyFiltered request attribute before doFilterInternal and removes it in a finally, so the INCLUDE/FORWARD dispatchers in webapp/src/main/webapp/WEB-INF/web.xml:163-170 do not re-run the body per JSP include. The one-line ask: have line 63's comment name the real consumers (or say so on the ticket), so the next person acting on TRUNK-6701's second half does not delete a live cross-module contract. Was it left deliberately for that reason?

what_i_swept:
Three passes, all inside performance.
PASS 1 - is the claimed saving real, and is it measured? Ran the decisive experiment rather than reasoning: swapped the merge-base OpenmrsFilter.java into the head worktree (`git show eda229b12a28a41ba35ecd75b910803da93631a8:web/src/main/java/org/openmrs/web/filter/OpenmrsFilter.java > ...`) and ran `mvn -o -pl web test -Dtest=OpenmrsFilterTest`. 3 of 5 fail on base with exactly the counts the PR claims to remove: shouldNotRewriteUnchangedAnonymousSessionAttributes expected 0 but was 1, shouldNotRewriteUnchangedAuthenticatedSessionAttributes expected 0 but was 2, shouldSetAuthenticatedUsernameAndLocale expected 1 but was 2. Restored with `git checkout --` and re-ran: 5/5 green, worktree clean. So the saving is real and quantified: per top-level request in steady state, 1 (anonymous) or 2 (authenticated) 'username' writes plus 1 'locale' write go to zero, and the authenticated case loses its write-anonymous-then-overwrite pair. It is also properly measured -- OpenmrsFilterTest's RecordingHttpSession counts setAttribute calls per key, which is an operation count rather than a timing, the right form of evidence here. Nothing to comment on; verified-clean earns silence.
PASS 2 - does the new code add work of its own to the same hot path? Read off the head file: +2 HttpSession.getAttribute and +2 Objects.equals per request, and getAuthenticatedUser() is now also called on the fresh-UserContext branch (a null field read). Net strictly fewer mutations in steady state; strictly more work only on a session's very first request (2 misses + 2 sets vs 2-3 sets), amortised to nothing. Then checked whether the guard's own inputs are expensive: UserContext.getAuthenticatedUser() (api/.../UserContext.java:211) is a bare field return; UserContext.getLocale() (UserContext.java:349) falls through to LocaleUtility.getDefaultLocale(), which I read in full (LocaleUtility.java:57-97) -- double-checked locking on a `static volatile Locale defaultLocaleCache` (line 37, correctly volatile), so after warm-up it is a volatile read. I chased the one branch that would have made it costly: line 88-91 returns fromSpecification(...) WITHOUT caching when Context.isSessionOpen() is false, and Context.isSessionOpen() (Context.java:970) is `userContextHolder.get() != null`, which OpenmrsFilter only satisfies at line 106, AFTER the locale read at line 94. That would be an uncached locale parse on every anonymous request -- but it only fires while defaultLocaleCache is null, and Listener.java:602 opens a Context session at startup, so it is a transient window after a default-locale GP change, not steady state. Candidate dropped: it does not hold, and in any case the call count is identical before and after.
PASS 3 - trace outward. (a) Invocation multiplicity: web.xml maps OpenmrsFilter to /* with INCLUDE and FORWARD dispatchers, which would multiply the per-request work across JSP portlet includes; disassembled spring-web 7.0.9 OncePerRequestFilter.doFilter with javap -c and confirmed the alreadyFiltered request attribute is set before doFilterInternal and removed in a finally, so the body runs once per top-level request. (b) Consumers of the two attributes, in-repo and downstream: `git grep` plus org-wide `gh search code` for setAttribute("locale"/"username") and getAttribute("locale"/"username"). No module writes either session key per request; the only module hits are pageContext.setAttribute in JSP footers, which is page scope, not session. (c) Guard-defeat scenario: if any other writer stored a String under "locale", Objects.equals(String, Locale) would never match and the new code would be a small net loss (+2 reads, same writes). core does have a second writer of the same key -- FilterUtil.LOCALE_ATTRIBUTE = "locale" (FilterUtil.java:36), written as a String by InitializationFilter and UpdateFilter -- but those are setup/upgrade handlers, not per-request, so the session converges after one write. Refuted, not shipped. (d) Listeners: the saving's real mechanism in a container is that setAttribute fires HttpSessionAttributeListeners and dirties the session; `git grep` shows core registers HttpSessionListener only (web/src/main/java/org/openmrs/web/Listener.java:78), no attribute listeners, so on a single node the saving is a couple of map puts. It matters in the clustered/replicated deployments the ticket names, which nothing here exercises. (e) Mutable session state: UserContext is stored as a session attribute and mutated in place, so its mutations were never replicated either before or after -- pre-existing, and I confirmed the PR neither helps nor hurts it. (f) CI cost of the new test class: it extends BaseWebContextSensitiveTest exactly as GZIPFilterTest/InitializationFilterTest/UpdateFilterTest/FilterUtilTest do, carries no @DirtiesContext, and its dataset is a single users row, so it reuses the cached Spring context and adds no new context startup.

out_of_scope: FilterUtil.LOCALE_ATTRIBUTE (web/src/main/java/org/openmrs/web/filter/util/FilterUtil.java:36) is the literal string "locale" -- the same session key OpenmrsFilter writes -- but InitializationFilter/UpdateFilter store a String there while OpenmrsFilter stores a Locale object: one key, two types (correctness/convention).

OpenmrsFilter.doFilterInternal calls httpRequest.getSession() unconditionally on a /* mapping, creating an HTTP session for every anonymous static-asset hit; the ticket explicitly scopes session-creation behaviour out, so I did not develop it.

UserContext is a mutable Serializable stored as a session attribute and mutated in place by authenticate/logout/setLocale with no re-setAttribute, so a replicating session manager never sees those mutations -- pre-existing and unchanged by this PR.
The stale-looking comment at OpenmrsFilter.java:63 ("used by htmlInclude tag") is in fact accurate: HtmlIncludeTag lives in openmrs-module-legacyui, outside this repo.
could_not_verify: No clustered or session-replicating container is available here, so the ticket's headline motivation (not marking the session dirty for replicating session managers) is established from write counts, not measured against a real DeltaManager/Spring Session deployment.

`gh search code --owner openmrs` indexes only default branches of public repos in that org, so a private or out-of-org module could still write "locale"/"username" on the session per request and permanently defeat the new guard, which would turn the change into a small net loss (+2 getAttribute per request, same number of writes). I found no evidence of such a writer, and core's own second writer of that key is setup-only.

No wall-clock timing was attempted. The brief states this machine is running five concurrent agents and that timings are untrustworthy, so every quantitative claim above is an operation count, not a duration.
notes: Bottom line for my dimension: the saving is real, correctly shaped, and locked in by tests that fail on the merge base -- I verified all three by running them, not by reading. The absolute size is small on a single node (a couple of ConcurrentHashMap puts on a request path that already opens a Hibernate session via OpenSessionInViewFilter for every static asset); the win concentrates in replicated-session deployments, which is exactly what the ticket said and is the part nobody can measure from this repo. I considered and rejected an approach objection: the alternative shape (write username/locale only at authenticate/logout/setLocale time, so the per-request check disappears entirely) is not reachable, because UserContext lives in the api module and has no handle on the HttpSession. The chosen guard is the minimal shape available in scope, so per the skill's rule an approach I agree with earns no comment. My single finding is non-blocking and is really about the half of TRUNK-6701 that did not ship and must not ship -- worth a line on the record so it is not 'fixed' later.
